title: Brick-and-Mortar Store Opening Feasibility & Break-Even Model

listing.description_html:
Total up what opening a shop really costs, ramp the sales over 24 months, and see the break-even sales, the first profitable month, the payback month and the cash you must have before you sign the lease.

You enter the build-out, inventory, deposits and other startup costs, the sales you expect when the shop is mature, how long the ramp takes and the percentage of mature sales you will make in month one, plus gross margin, rent, payroll and other costs.

What's included

  • Startup cost total with contingency and a working-capital reserve
  • 24-month sales ramp, gross profit, variable and fixed costs
  • Break-even sales per month and as a share of mature sales
  • First profitable month, payback month and the deepest cash hole
  • Year-two profit and return on the total funding
  • A guide with scenarios, a lease-signing checklist, a routine and an FAQ

Who it's for

  • First-time shop, cafe, boutique and studio owners
  • Franchise and pop-up operators evaluating a second location
  • Business-plan writers and loan applicants who need a defensible break-even
  • Landlords' tenants negotiating rent-free months and fit-out allowances

You get: store_opening_feasibility_break_even_model.xlsx (Inputs, Months, Summary) and a PDF guide.

Works in Excel 2016 or later, Excel for Mac and Excel on the web; opens in Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

This workbook is a calculation tool, not business, lending, legal or financial advice. Every output depends on the estimates you enter; retail sales ramps are uncertain and most new shops need more cash and more time than planned. Verify your costs with quotes and your lease terms with a lawyer.

pricing_evidence.basis: Two sources. (1) Web searches run on 2026-11-05 through a search index (summaries, not purchases): external_observations, only what a result actually showed; a missing price is null. (2) The factory's own catalogue tiers. No price here is validated by buyers.

pricing_evidence.rationale: $39: a 24-month feasibility model with a long guide; placed above the $9-24 single-purpose calculators and with the factory's other multi-sheet models.
pricing_evidence.demand: WAITING FOR REAL DATA: the account has 0 sales on 112 listings, so no price here is validated by buyers.
pricing_evidence.market_position: Simple break-even tools are free or a few dollars; retail-specific models exist but their prices were not visible. $39 is above every visible price and is price-exposed.
